title: Wire EDM: arcs in taper (conical) mode

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
## What happens

A Wire Contour with a taper does not cut a DXF arc as an arc. The selected-chain path refuses a taper on a DXF chain ("selected DXF wire cuts require a single vertical pass"). The wire posts refuse a tapered arc ("a tapered arc - the wire post writes straight tapered moves only"). The verifier reads an arc on a leaning wire as unreadable.

The fix for #3937 cuts vertical arcs as true G2 / G3 arcs. Tapered arcs stay refused on purpose. The maintainer decided that this is rare work (24 Nov 2026).

## Why it is a separate issue

A tapered arc is a cone. The lower and the upper arc have different radii. Each control states a conical arc in its own way. Some controls refuse two arcs in a row in conical mode. Each dialect needs evidence from its control before a post writes such a block.

## What is expected

- The generator lays a tapered arc as a cone: the lower arc and the upper arc, each with its own radius.
- The wire laws and the verifier read the cone against the drawing.
- Each wire post that supports conical arcs writes them. Each other post refuses them by name, as now.

## Related

- #3937 (vertical arcs on DXF chains).
- #3215 (wire output writes no arcs).
- #2702 (G-EDM XYUV taper).

## Labels

The account that files this issue cannot set labels. A collaborator: please set `P8`, `effort:max`, `area:post`, `area:2d`, `source:agent`.

Done means: a tapered DXF arc cuts as a cone on each post that has control evidence, and each other post refuses it by name.

title: Live MCP: make the idle timeout configurable (the 5-minute drop ends a stdio client's session)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
## What happens

The app runs with `--mcp-port 7878`, and an MCP client that only launches stdio servers (Claude Code) drives it through `camcraft-cli mcp --connect 127.0.0.1:7878`.

After 300 s without a request, the app closes the client (`IDLE_TIMEOUT` in `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs`, from #567):

```
mcp: client 127.0.0.1:53042 dropped: idle - no complete line for 300.0s; serving the next client
```

The bridge (`crates/app/src/mcp/bridge.rs`) exits when the app closes its side. The client then reports the server as disconnected, and the user has to restart it by hand. A 5-minute pause is common in a real CAM session: the user reads the agent's answer or checks the model in the window, or the agent writes notes between calls. In one session on 0.25.0 it dropped several times. The document stays open in the window, so nothing is lost, but every reconnect is manual.

## Request

Make the idle window configurable, matching `--mcp-port` / `CAMCRAFT_MCP_PORT`:

- `--mcp-idle-timeout <seconds>` and `CAMCRAFT_MCP_IDLE_TIMEOUT`
- `0` = never drop an idle client
- default stays 300 s, so #567's behaviour doesn't change

`Inbox::listen_with_idle` already takes the window, so this looks like CLI and environment plumbing only.

## Related, optional

The bridge could also reconnect on the next request instead of exiting (replaying the client's `initialize`). That would make a drop invisible to the client whatever the timeout is.

**Version:** CamCraft 0.25.0 (Arch package), Linux.

title: Tool meridian of a sharp taper or a drill misses the radial shoulder when the flute is shorter than the cone

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

`Tool::meridian()` (`crates/tools/src/meridian.rs`) and `Tool::profile()` disagree for a sharp tapered mill or a drill when the flute length is shorter than the cone. The profile steps out to the full radius at the flute top. The meridian does not add that radial shoulder, so it ends at a smaller radius.

The review of PR #3929 found this class for flat and ball taper tips (review comment 7144791597). PR #3929 fixes it for the new flat and ball tips only (`crates/tools/src/taper.rs`, `meridian_points`). It does not change sharp tapers or drills, because that PR keeps their output byte-identical. The same missing shoulder stays on `main` for sharp tapers and drills.

## Why it matters

The two shapes describe the same tool. If code reads the meridian for a collision, gouge, simulation or solid, it sees a smaller tool than the profile and the real cutter. That can hide a contact. The filer has not traced each reader of the meridian; this needs a check before the priority is set.

## What to check

- Each reader of the tool meridian for milling tools (sim tool bodies, solids, fidelity checks, stamps).
- A sharp taper and a drill with a flute shorter than the cone: compare `profile()` and `meridian()` at the flute top. A test in the style of `taper::tests::short_flat_profile_and_meridian_agree` (PR #3929) shows the gap.

## Done means

For every tool kind, the meridian and the profile agree at the flute top, including the radial shoulder of a short flute. A test pins a sharp taper and a drill with a short flute. Any changed digest or golden is listed in the PR.

The account that files this issue cannot set labels. A collaborator: please set the priority (P1 if a collision or gouge check reads the meridian, else P3), `bug`, an effort label, the area label and `source:agent`.

Found while fixing #3929.

body:
## What happens

A Wire EDM contour on a DXF chain that contains an arc or a circle fails to generate. The maintainer reported it.

```
generate failed: could not generate the toolpath: Wire Contour1: invalid machining parameters: the selected DXF chain contains an arc or circle; the generic wire path requires straight segments
```

The refusal is made at `crates/app/src/operation/wire_sketch.rs:247`.

## Why it matters

A circle and an arc are the most common wire EDM shapes: a punch, a die opening, a hole. The generic wire path cannot cut either one. This blocks the basic use of the wire feature. The maintainer set the priority at `P1`.

## What is expected

- The wire path accepts an arc and a circle from the DXF chain.
- The path is cut as an arc: a wire machine interpolates an arc from its own block (G02/G03 with I/J or R), so the toolpath and the post carry the arc, not a long chord list.
- A full circle without a lead-in point has a start rule (a lead-in on the circle, or a slit), and the path says which.

## Related issues

- #3215: "Wire output writes no arcs: circles and fillets become G01 chords". The output side of the same class. This issue is the generation side.
- #3216: Wire Contour closing overlap, centre-line slit cutting, skims on open contours.
- #2702: G-EDM XYUV taper and 4-axis ruled wire post support.
- #2692: XYUV wire EDM swallowtail test fixtures.
- #2871: Example case: Wire Contour, and a taper that the machine refuses.

## What to check

- The refusal at `wire_sketch.rs:247`: which chain kinds reach it, and whether the generic path has an arc arm at all.
- The wire post vocabulary: a dialect that writes an arc block (G02/G03 with I/J) and the one that accepts only G01.
- The pin `crates/app/tests/wire_dxf_selection.rs:219` asserts the refusal. It changes when the feature lands.

## Missing at filing

- The DXF and the operation parameters. Add them as a comment when the case is reproduced.

body:
## What happens

With "Pass starts at" Outside, every strategy makes a strange clearing pattern of straight lines.

- The pattern does not follow the shape of the stock edge.
- The pattern does not follow the selected edge.
- The tool lifts more than it must.

The maintainer reported this. He set the priority at `P1`.

## What is expected

- The first passes blend from straight lines into curves. The shape follows the selected edge as the pass gets closer to the part.
- The pass follows the stock edge as long as it stays outside the part.
- The tool stays down when a link is clear. It lifts only where the cut needs it.

## Why it matters

- The path is slow and it is not the shape that the user selects.
- The unnecessary lifts cost time and leave marks.
- On a P1, a wrong path can also cut the stock edge in the wrong place.

## What to check

- The Outside start plan of each strategy: which geometry does it use for the first passes, the stock outline or the part offset?
- The blend from a straight lead to the part offset: where is the ring built, and does it taper the distance to the selected edge?
- The link and lift rule of the first passes: is a lift made although the chord is clear?
- The pins: `pass_start_*`, `offset_pass_start` and the catalog cases may assert the straight-line pattern as correct.

## Related

- #3932 (2D Adaptive trochoidal slots to a wall, no outside start).
- #3933 (2D Pocket offset rings behave like waterline).
- #3928 (2D Offset Outside ramp only with Arc turn corners).

## Missing at filing

title: 2D Adaptive trochoidal: slots to a wall instead of walking the contour, and no outside start

body:
## What happens

The 2D Adaptive strategy does not adapt to the free space. With trochoidal passes it walks the path in the wrong way:

- It makes straight slots until the tool reaches a wall. The slot is at the full width of the tool.
- It does not walk the selected edge with trochoidal moves.
- It cannot start from the outside of the part.

The maintainer reported this while cutting a part with the 2D Adaptive strategy.

## What is expected

- The trochoidal pass follows the selected contour, like a spiral along the edge, with small trochoidal loops.
- The step and the loop width adapt to the space that is free at each point.
- The operation can start from the outside of the stock.

## Why it matters

- The full-width slots load the tool. The strategy exists to keep the engagement small.
- The current path is slow, and it does not cut the shape that the user selected.
- Without an outside start, the entry is inefficient on an open edge.

## What to check

- The engagement limit: the loop width and the step must come from it at each point, not only at the first pass.
- The pass layout of the adaptive strategy: does it fall back to slotting when the island or the wall is near?
- The start side: the strategy must accept an Outside start on an open edge.
- The pins: `adaptive_troch_*` and the example catalog cases may not cover an open edge with a near wall.

## Missing at filing

- The sketch, the tool, the stock and the posted program. Add them as a comment when the case is reproduced.

If any of these slots can gouge the part or the fixture, this issue is `P1`. Confirm on the fixture first.

title: 2D Contour under carried stock: a tab window peck bites more than one stepdown

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
## What happens

A 2D Contour with its top below the stock top (carried stock) pecks a later tab window dive from the wrong floor. The first peck bites more than one stepdown of stock.

Steps (found during #3925):

1. Load `examples/catalog/2d/contour-tabs/contour-tabs.camproj`.
2. Set the contour `top_z` offset to `-4.0` (top of stock reference). The stock top is Z 6, the stepdown is 2 mm, the levels are Z 2 and Z 0.
3. Generate.

Result: each of the three later tab windows of the last level pecks Z 2, then Z 0. The first peck feeds from the stock top Z 6 to Z 2: a 4 mm bite. The verifier names each one as `PlungeTooDeep { mm: 4.0, limit_mm: 2.0 }`. The ring start dive to Z 2 also bites 4 mm.

## Cause

`contour_peck` (#3678) reads the floor with no cut as "the material top, or one stepdown over the ring's first level where that is lower". Under carried stock the material above the op's top is real. The floor is then Z 4, not Z 6.

## Notes

- Nothing gouges and nothing collides. The risk is the tool load.
- The generator note "Carried stock" and the verifier note name the deep bite. The post is not held.
- The ring start dive to the first level does not peck by design (#3678).
- `crates/app/tests/plunge_depth_tab.rs` `a_tabbed_contour_under_carried_stock_names_its_deep_dives` pins the current behaviour. A fix changes that test on purpose.

## Done means

- A later window dive under carried stock pecks from the real stock top, one stepdown at a time, or the choice to keep the current floor is recorded in `docs/decisions/`.

body:
**Problem.** The built-in holder library (`crates/tools/src/holder_library*.rs`) has these holders:

- BT30, BT40 and CAT40, each with an ER collet chuck and a Weldon side-lock version;
- standalone ER11-ER40 collet chucks;
- Tormach TTS (ER20 and Weldon).

Many common spindle tapers and clamping types are missing. A user with such a machine must draw the holder (tool editor, #93) or import a DXF outline. Collision checks and simulation then depend on a hand-made shape.

**Missing, most common first:**

1. **HSK**: A63, E40, E32 and F63. These are common on routers and newer mills.
2. **SK / ISO / DIN 69871** (SK30, SK40) and **ISO 20/25/30** (automatic tool change router spindles).
3. **R8**: manual and small CNC knee mills.
4. **Shrink-fit holders** on the tapers above.

Then: CAT30, CAT50 and BT50; Morse taper; NMTB; hydraulic and milling (end-mill) chucks; ER50 and TG collets.

**Rules for each holder** (the same as `holder_library.rs`):

- Take the dimensions from the published standard dimension tables. Record each number and its source in a `docs/decisions/` file.
- Draw a conservative, typical outline: never smaller than the steel. Do not copy a vendor model.
- Add tests in the same form as `holder_library_tests.rs`.

This is under the safety floor, because the holder outline goes into the collision and gouge checks (`effort:high`).

**Coordination.** Do this together with qsmits's Tool library work: #3897 (U6, Holders list and holder view) and #3895 (U4, holder, stick-out and gauge length). Also see #3648 (component library and compatible-holder filter). Add a new holder type in the shape that U6 uses, so that the holder list shows it.

**Done means:** each holder in groups 1-4 is in the built-in library, with its standard source in a decision file and a pinning test. It can be selected for a tool in the tool library window. Users can add more holder types, as follow-ups, in this issue's comments.

title: 2D Contour: with a Linear lead-in, the first descent stands on the cutter-centre line, before G41/G42 engages

labels.name: bug

labels.name: area:2d

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

With a Linear lead-in and control or wear compensation, the plunge point of the first descent lies on the extension of the centre path. The tool edge is tangent to the finished wall at that point. The clearance to the wall is 0.000 mm. The descent runs before G41/G42 engages, so the posted program has no compensation at that move.

At nominal tool size the tool touches nothing at this point. A real tool larger than the nominal size would touch the wall. With a Perpendicular lead-in the same descent is one lead length away from the wall.

## Reading

Setup: Side Outside, entry Plunge, no transition, control and wear compensation, tool diameter 6 mm, stock to leave 0, top Z 0, bottom Z -4, stepdown 2, climb, lead length 3 mm. The part is three 16 mm squares, 30 mm apart. Clearance is the distance from the descent end points to the wall, minus the nominal radius (3.000 mm).

| Lead-in | Descents before G41/G42 | Least clearance to the wall |
|---|---|---|
| Linear 3 mm | 6 | 0.000 mm (all 6) |
| Perpendicular 3 mm | 6 | 3.000 mm (all 6) |

The result is the same for control and for wear compensation. The wall-side generator does not use the bore-side entry code, and this finding does not depend on a ring entry. The bore side (Side Inside) with a Linear lead-in reads 0.000 mm too, for Plunge and for Arc entry. It is the same on main.

## Where

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/arc_leads.rs:26-29`: `lead_in` returns the plunge point `s - t*length` for a Linear lead. That point is on the centre path's own edge. A Perpendicular lead returns `s + air*length` (lines 22-25).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_comp.rs`: `door` and `push_span`. The span starts at the lead-in move. The moves before it are G40, at the nominal centre.
- `docs/decisions/3888-ramp-comp-refusal.md:23-26`: "The dive at the lead-in's start, which the door's lead-length law keeps at least one radius off the ring, stays legal."

The premise of that sentence holds for a Perpendicular lead-in (3.000 mm). It does not hold for a Linear lead-in (0.000 mm). The sentence is not about a Linear lead-in, and no other file says that the 0.000 mm is by design.

## Not known

I did not measure a real tool larger than the register value on a machine. The reading is from the generated path only.

## Expected

One of these:
- The descent for a Linear lead-in stands at least some stated distance off the wall, as for a Perpendicular lead-in.
- Or the decision file and the lead-in documentation state that a Linear lead-in descent is tangent to the wall, so a user can choose a Perpendicular lead-in.

## Done means

- A test with a Linear lead-in and control compensation names the least clearance of the descents before the first G41/G42, and pins the chosen rule.
- The decision file for #3888 states the rule for both lead-in types.

Refs #3888, #3890.

## What happens

An outside 2D Contour with entry Ramp or Helix enters its first ring by the entry. PR #3833 ramps the first ring of each level on the wall side.

Each ring after the first ring at the same level is reached through the pass link. `contour_link::ring_link` lifts, crosses and plunges straight down at the plunge feed. The posted program has an axial dive at each of these rings. No note says so.

This is the same fault as #3830 on the bore side. PR #3834 fixes the bore side only.

## Reading

Setup: no compensation, tool diameter 6 mm, stepdown 1 mm, 3 levels, bottom Z -3, ramp angle 5 degrees. Each part is a 16 mm square. The parts are 40 mm apart. Counts are plunge moves / axial dives, measured on a branch that has #3833.

| Entry | 1 part | 2 separate parts | 3 separate parts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ramp 5 degrees | 0 / 0 | 3 / 3 | 6 / 6 |
| Plunge | 3 / 3 | 6 / 6 | 9 / 9 |

Ramp and Helix post no note about these dives. Helix posts only its stand-down note.

## Where

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour.rs`: `ring_to_ring`, then `ring_link`. The bore side asks for the entry. The wall side does not.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_link.rs`: `ring_link`, the lines after the keep-down proof (`guard`, then `MoveKind::Plunge`).

## Expected

One of these:
- Each ring after the first ring takes the entry (ramp or helix), by the wall-side ramp of #3833.
- Or the generator names the plunge in a note, as the bore side does for the tabbed case.

The compensation refusal of #3890 stays: control and wear compensation refuse Ramp and Helix on both sides.

- A test with n separate parts and entry Ramp shows no axial dive and no plunge move. It fails on main.

title: Research: keep face picks on a SolidCraft model after a design change, with the face names in the `.sc` model cache

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: needs-research
labels.description: Large idea with open questions: research and file sub-issues before any code

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
**What happens now**

An operation picks faces on a model. CamCraft stores each face pick as a hash of the face geometry: the plane, the outline segments, the loops and the area (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature.rs:880-900`, `crates/app/src/project/file.rs:756-758` on `main` `02bf65d93`).

A linked `.sc` model imports again when its file changes (#2463). Then:

- a pick on a face that did not change stays;
- a pick on a face that moved or changed size is refused at generate: "Face of 'part' is no longer in the model: re-pick it".

I saw both on 0.26.0 (2026-11-24): a top face moved from Z15 to Z17, and the operation on it needed a new pick. So each design change that touches a picked face needs a new pick by hand.

**What the `.sc` file already holds**

- SolidCraft keeps the face names of each body in the model cache. `docs/design-container.md`, section "Model cache", says that face names are recorded in the cache. The SolidCraft project has the MIT OR Apache-2.0 licence.
- In a test file in this repository, `testdata/models/solidcraft_for_beginners.sc`, the names are in `cache/model.json`, at `model.names[].faces`. An example is `"F2:side:l13"`.
- The names come from the feature history of the design. SolidCraft's own `model.faces` command gives each face its `name` and an `exact` flag. `exact: false` means that SolidCraft found the name from the geometry.
- CamCraft already reads this cache through SolidCraft's published source (`crates/kernel/src/solidcraft/cache.rs`). It reads only the final body record, not the names.

**Proposal (the need, not the code)**

- When a model comes from a `.sc` file, keep the SolidCraft face name beside each face pick.
- After the model imports again, find the face by its name first.
- The geometry still decides. If the named face is now of a different kind (for example, a plane became a cylinder), refuse as today, and give the name in the message.
- A model with no names (STEP, OBJ, STL, an older `.sc`) or a name with `exact: false`: the same behaviour as today.
- A project that does not use this does not change.

**Open questions (research before code)**

1. Do the names in `model.names[].faces` come in the same order as the faces of the body record in `cache/bodies.bin`? Does SolidCraft document this order, or is it only in its source?
2. CamCraft picks welded faces that it builds from the facets. Can each welded face keep its source face (or faces) of the body record through tessellation and welding? What happens when one welded face covers two source faces, or one source face splits into two welded faces?
3. Where does the name go:
   - on the pick in the project file, as an optional field, with or without a `PROJECT_VERSION` step;
   - or in a table on the model, which the pick refers to?
4. What does a pick do when its name is not in the new model (the face was deleted), or when two faces have the name (a split)? A proposal: refuse and give the name, as today.
5. Edges and chains: do the same with edge names (SolidCraft also names edges), or faces only at first?
6. How does this fit #3817 (advisory feature data from `document.json`)? Both read SolidCraft's published container. One reader can serve both.
7. Which tests pin it? A proposal: a pair of `.sc` fixtures (one design, before and after a dimension change), with a pick that stays by name and a pick whose face is gone.

**Who benefits**

Each user who programs a SolidCraft part and then changes the design. This includes a version-control or part-database workflow, where each new version of a part comes in as a new file. SolidCraft's RFC 0001 (`docs/rfcs/0001-craft-bridge.md`, phase 2) asks for the same result through an exchange file that does not exist yet. The `.sc` cache has the names now, so CamCraft can do this with no change in SolidCraft.

**Done means:** a research comment answers these questions, and concrete sub-issues are filed (AGENTS.md "needs-research").

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

body:
**Problem.** Two tasks have no written procedure:

1. Take over a stalled PR of a different author.
2. Reproduce a bug before the fix starts.

Agents do these tasks now with no fixed steps. The results are not the same each time.

**Prior art.** SolidCraft (Apache-2.0) has the skills `solidcraft-takeover` and `solidcraft-repro-first` in `.agents/skills/`. Use them for ideas only. Write our own text, and obey our rules (claims, "Refresh only at merge time", maintainer edits).

**Proposal.**

- `takeover` skill:
  - Do a takeover only when the author approves it, or when the claim is stale by **A claim must be live**.
  - Do not push while the author is active.
  - Push to the author's branch with maintainer edits. If GitHub refuses the push, post the patch as a comment.
  - Write one comment that names the commits and the reason.
- `repro-first` skill:
  - Reproduce the bug through MCP or a pinned test before you write the fix.
  - Record the reading from before the fix in the PR body.
  - If the bug does not reproduce on the latest `main`, stop. Post the evidence on the issue.

**Done means:** the two skills are in `.claude/skills/`, and the "How to read this file" table in `AGENTS.md` names them. The PR body has `Process change: yes`.

Related: the developer page for agent contributors (PR #3911).

title: Tool library file: .camtools drops the drawn cutter (ToolCutter) on export and import

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
**What happens**

A tool can have a drawn cutter outline (`ToolCutter`, #93 slice 2). The project file (`.camproj`) keeps it in `ToolDto::cutter`. The tool library file (`.camtools`) does not keep it:

- `export_tool_library` (`crates/app/src/tool_library.rs`, lines 94-129) writes the tool, its `body` or `holder`, and no `cutter`.
- `parse_tool_library` (lines 137-191) does not read a `cutter` key. `LibraryTool` has no cutter field.
- `ImportTools` (`crates/app/src/commands/tool_import/mod.rs`) sets the tool and its body only.

Thus an export and an import give a tool without its drawn cutter.

**Expected**

- Export writes the drawn cutter of each tool that has one, as `[z, r, arc]` points (the `.camproj` form).
- Import reads it and judges it against the tool numbers (`tool_body_wire::cutter_from_dto`, the same check as the project loader). A cutter that disagrees refuses the whole file by tool name.
- `ImportTools` Add, Update and Replace set the cutter, and undo restores the previous cutter, in one undo step.
- A file with a cutter says a new version (5). An older build then refuses the file by version. It does not drop the cutter silently.
- A file without a cutter keeps version 4 or lower, so older builds still read it.

**Why it matters**

- Since #852 the stack laws read the drawn neck of a cutter. A tool that loses its cutter in a library round trip is a different tool for those laws.
- The form mill kind (#3369, plan step D2) keeps its outline in this field. Without this fix, a form mill exported to a library loses its shape.
- This is a leftover of #93 (see the research comment on #93, item 4).

**Done means:** a tool with a drawn cutter makes the same tool after export and import; a cutter that disagrees refuses the file by name; Update replaces the cutter in one undo step; a library without a cutter keeps version 4 or lower. Pinned by tests in `crates/app/tests/tool_library.rs`.

Part of #3663 (plan step D3a). Refs #93.

The filer (qsmits) cannot set labels. A collaborator: please set a priority and an effort label, and `source:agent`. The parent #3663 is `P4`. This changes a file format, thus `effort:high` by the AGENTS.md effort table.

title: UI link: a client without the token can hold the only link session for 5 minutes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found in a security review of PR #3861 (part 1 of #3751).

**What happens**

The UI link serves one client at a time. The token check is on the first line, but the same deadlines apply before and after the token check:

- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs:181`: the link uses `IDLE_TIMEOUT` (5 minutes) for its listener.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs:233-255`: `accept_loop` serves clients one after the other.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs:283-351`: before the hello line, the read loop accepts up to `MAX_LINE` (16 MiB, line 56) and waits up to the idle window.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs:330-334`: the token check occurs only when a complete line arrives.

On Windows the link is TCP on 127.0.0.1 (`crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:221-226`). Each local user can connect to that port. A client without the token can connect and send no newline. It then holds the only session for 5 minutes. It can connect again after the drop. During that time, `camcraft-cli --ui` cannot reach the window. The app also buffers up to 16 MiB for an unauthenticated client.

No command runs, and the UI thread does not stop. This is a denial of service of the link only.

**Expected**

A client that does not send a valid hello line in a short time (for example 5 s) is closed. The hello line has a small size limit (for example 4 KiB). The 5-minute idle window and the 16 MiB limit apply only after the token check.

**Done means**

- A pre-hello deadline and a pre-hello size limit exist in `listen.rs`.
- A test in `crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs` connects, sends no hello, and shows that a second client with the token gets a session after the short deadline.

Refs #3751, PR #3861.

title: Column stock: simulate copies the whole cut history on each call, so a program cut one move at a time is quadratic

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

`stock_sim::cut::simulate` (the column engine behind `Stock::simulate`) copies the stock's whole cut history at the start of each call:

```rust
let mut history = dex.history.as_deref().cloned();
```

The history holds every cut so far. It grows with each call. A caller that cuts a program in small steps (one move for each call) thus copies a longer history at each step. The total time is quadratic in the number of moves.

Expected: the time of a program cut one move for each call is near the time of the same program cut in one call.

### Evidence

We run `camcraft-sim` from a fork as the stock engine of a batch verifier. The verifier reads the stock before each cutting move, thus it cuts one move for each call.

- A 3-axis job on a 2541 x 2100 column stock, 137,940 moves: one call takes 2 s. One move for each call ran for more than 1800 s, and we stopped it.
- With the history grown in place (below), one move for each call takes 6 s. The removed volume is the same to the bit as the one-call cut.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Make a column stock: `Stock::block(Backend::Column, 0.0, 0.0, 20.0, 20.0, 10.0, 0.1)`.
2. Make 4000 short feed moves across the block.
3. Cut them in one `simulate` call. Then cut them on a second, new block with one `simulate` call for each move.
4. Compare the times. The second cut is much slower, and the gap grows with the number of moves.

### Proposed fix

Take the history out of the stock, grow it in place with `Arc::make_mut` (this copies it only when another stock shares it), and put it back. On a refusal, truncate the cuts to their old count and put the history back, so the stock stays as it was (`add_ops` only appends cuts). We have this change and a pinning test on our fork. We will open a PR from a branch `issue/3819-history-in-place` if you accept the claim.

Not in scope: `carried::clip_columns_under` uses the same copy, but it runs one time for each setup, not for each move.

### Version and OS

v0.26.0 (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `P3` (slow with a workaround: cut in one call), `effort:high` (stock simulation is under the safety floor).

Done means: a pinning test in `camcraft-sim` cuts 4000 moves one call at a time on a column stock. Each column top is the same to the bit as the one-call cut, and the time stays inside a linear budget.

Before #3453 (origin/main 44c13a01d), PLANAR links:

| level | window | entry XY | plunge Z | floor under centre | disc floor | below disc floor | crescent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| -18 | 0 | (46.000, 8.865) | 2 -> -18 | -15.3 | 0 | 18.0 | 2.501 |
| -18 | 1 | (10.153, -6.000) | 12 -> -18 | -15.3 | 0 | 18.0 | 2.501 |
| -18 | 2 | (-6.000, 29.525) | 12 -> -18 | -15.3 | 0 | 18.0 | 2.501 |
| -18 | 3 | (21.000, 30.029) | 12 -> -18 | -15.3 | 0 | 18.0 | 2.501 |

After the #3453 PR (window 0 enters at the untabbed start; the tab layout ends the tabs on the spacing marks from the start), PLANAR links:

| level | window | entry XY | plunge Z | floor under centre | disc floor | below disc floor | crescent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| -18 | 0 | (43.514, -5.802) | 2 -> -18 | -15.3 | -15.3 | 2.7 | 0 |
| -18 | 1 | (-5.165, -4.266) | 12 -> -18 | 0 | 0 | 18.0 | full disc |
| -18 | 2 | (-4.796, 44.676) | 12 -> -18 | 0 | 0 | 18.0 | full disc |
| -18 | 3 | (18.186, 19.500) | 12 -> -18 | -15.3 | -15.3 | 2.7 | 0 |

With the stay-down ramp preset (`level: KeepDown`, `transition: Ramp`), the untabbed levels below the first do not cut the lead-in. After #3453, window 0 of the -18 level plunges 2 -> -18 at (43.514, -5.802) with the disc floor at -4.5: 13.5 mm below the floor.

### What happens

FAIL  ui suites: lib  exit 101
process didn't exit successfully: `...\camcraft_ui-b30d80154151484e.exe --test-threads=12` (exit code: 0xc0000005, STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION)

test result: ok. 1425 passed; 0 failed; 7 ignored; finished in 166.04s

title: STEP import removes a short edge from a Fusion solid and then refuses the enlarged gap

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happens

CamCraft refuses a Fusion STEP model of a heater block. The user reproduced the failure in the desktop app on macOS (v0.24.0, commit `e6e04f5d0`). The MCP tool `import_model` gives the same result. Two AP214 exports and one AP242 export contain the same edge geometry. All three give this diagnostic:

```text
import_model: corrupt STEP: solidcore: import_step produced an invalid result: 1 of 1 solid item(s) refused; first #14 at check: a vertex sits 1.157e-2 mm off its edges (limit 1e-3) - re-export the model, or import an STL
```

The user can view an STL copy. A STEP copy exported from FreeCAD gives the same gap. The original CAD files stay local.

### Where the gap comes from

A diagnostic probe built the same STEP record twice with the pinned Solidcore version (`2016386`). Only the healing setting changed.

| Measurement | Before healing | After normal import healing |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Edges in the solid | 999 | 998 |
| Gap at the start of spline edge `#3375` | 0.006223 mm | 0.011573 mm |
| Largest vertex-to-endpoint gap in the solid | 0.007736 mm | 0.011573 mm |

The file defines edge `#3407` between vertices `#2564` and `#2120`. The vertices are 0.009944 mm apart. Spline edge `#3375` starts at `#2564`. Healing removes `#3407` and redirects `#3375` to `#2120`. Measuring from that vertex to the same spline endpoint reproduces the reported gap. The diagnostic names the solid (`#14`), so the user cannot identify the affected edge.

FreeCAD (Open CASCADE) keeps both vertices and all 999 edges. It reports one valid, closed solid with 345 faces. The file declares 0.010 mm uncertainty.

### Two limits still apply

The largest gap before healing already exceeds CamCraft's fixed 0.001 mm vertex limit. A separate probe passed the reader's record to the machining mesher at the normal 0.005 mm chord target. The mesher refused face 0 with a measured deviation of 0.011141 mm. Increasing the vertex limit alone would still leave a mesh refusal.

### Decision requested

Can the importer preserve an explicit short edge when collapsing it increases the endpoint error on an adjacent edge? If the preserved solid still exceeds machining tolerance, should CamCraft offer a reduced-fidelity view or refuse it with the measured accuracy? Issue #2976 and PR #2994 provide a precedent for reduced fidelity on an edge-to-surface gap. This case concerns a vertex and a curve endpoint.

**Done means:** A synthetic STEP regression fixture covers two distinct vertices joined by a short edge beside a spline. The test checks the edge count and the endpoint error before and after healing. A second test pins the agreed import outcome when the source exceeds machining tolerance. The user can see which check failed and the measured gap. Machining checks continue to use the accuracy the importer achieved.

**Triage.** P3 because direct STEP import fails and an STL copy works for viewing. `effort:high` because the fix changes geometry repair and needs a regression test.

[STEP build and validation](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/e6e04f5d0/crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs#L297-L337) · [Vertex limit and measurement](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/e6e04f5d0/crates/kernel/src/solidcore_import.rs#L106-L157)

body:
## What happens

PR B of #917 (branch `issue/917-solidcore-step`) meshes STEP files through solidcore. The new mesh of `testdata/models/Milling-test.step` and `testdata/models/fig8.step` is finer. Three toolpath tests now fail. They pass on the head of #2843 (`eae027d55`). The PR marks them `known-fail #2849`. Their asserts do not change.

1. `lead_approach::the_horizontal_arc_entry_on_the_users_pocket_verifies_silent` (line 247). The stock-source pocket with `Entry3D::Helix` gives these notes:
   - `entry: the horizontal arc entry does not fit (...) - the entry descends onto the pass start without it`
   - `entry: the pass start (-31.878, 8.513) at Z 17.500 is in material and the helix fits only away from the pass start - ramp along the pass instead` (and the same at Z 15, 12.5, 10)
   - `2D Pocket: the check for corners of the stock tighter than the tool did not run (invalid geometry: loop crosses itself) - look at the stock corners around the part`
2. `lead_approach::an_axis_aligned_lead_start_posts_the_users_arc_entry_as_g18_or_g19` (line 131). The contour with `axis_start` gets no vertical arc. Notes:
   - `entry: oblique vertical arc posted as chords - no standard plane`
   - `depth: the ring at (-0.333, -7.491) ends at its floor Z 0.000 - the part is solid below it; levels below skipped (-5.000, -7.000)`
3. `shoulder_adaptive::fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works` (line 312). The last feed ends 31.406 mm from the part outline. The test expects 4 mm (the tool radius). The path verifies clean and posts.

## Safety

No result is silent wrong output. Tests 1 and 2 state each fallback in a note. Test 3 verifies clean. But the corner check in `crates/app/src/operation/keep_law.rs` does not run, and the user sees only the note.

## The defect

The "loop crosses itself" error comes from `Region::normalize` in `crates/geometry/src/geo2d.rs` (line 233). A region that the corner check builds from the new mesh outline has a self-crossing loop. Find which loop it is, and why the solidcore mesh makes it. Then check if tests 1 to 3 have the same cause.

## Done when

- The three tests pass with no change to their asserts.
- The `known-fail #2849` markers are removed.

title: STEP import refuses a legal file: a boundary point lies off a twisted B-spline surface

body:
## What the user sees

The import of a user STEP file with a twisted B-spline flank stops with this refusal:

`a boundary point lies off the surface, outside its knot domain`

The file is legal. A different tool that reads STEP through solidcore opens the same file. The file is private and is not attached.

## Where

- The refusal comes from `Fault::Outside` in `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_nearest.rs:112`.
- The import path is the truck-stepio path.

## Cause, as found

- The surface is a degree-3 B-spline surface with a strong twist.
- The Newton search for the nearest surface point lands on a neighbouring sheet of the surface.
- The rescue grid has 4 samples for each knot span. On this surface the grid is too coarse to find the correct sheet.
- The defect is of the same class as #1602.

## Possible fixes

- Import STEP through solidcore (#917). This is the full fix.
- Or make the rescue search denser, or make it use the trim boundary.

The work decides between these and records the decision.

## Done when

- A STEP fixture that we made, with a strongly twisted degree-3 B-spline face, imports without the refusal. The fixture is not the user's file.
- A boundary point that is off the surface by more than the tolerance still gives the refusal.
- The import does not become slower by a large factor on the current fixtures.

## Effort

The importer makes geometry. Thus the safety floor applies and the effort is `effort:high`.

Found while fixing #2719 (PR #2732).

What happens: when the curved-face fit cannot measure a face, the import reports the face `UNMEASURED` and the model is reduced fidelity. Verify then refuses each operation with `model_fidelity::TOO_COARSE`: "imported too coarsely to verify; re-import with a larger STEP facet budget". A larger facet budget does not help this face. Only the warn log line names the true cause (`step: face <n> keeps the kernel's facets unmeasured (<reason>)`).

Expected: the refusal names the cause, for example "a curved face of the model could not be measured", and does not advise a larger budget.

Option: measure the kept kernel mesh of that face with a nearest-point search (see `docs/decisions/2719-step-fit-fallback-diagnostic.md`). Then a fine kernel mesh stays at full fidelity.

Done means: the user-facing refusal for an unmeasured face names that cause, and a test pins the text.

Found by the QA runs of 2026-11-18 (SolidCraft v0.44.1 designs -> CamCraft main `83867fd7`), parts p06 (all-ops mill part) and p07 (lathe shaft); both have fillets or blend faces.

What happens: `import_model <design>.sc` refuses the design:
`Solidcraft design refused: import_solidcraft: invalid input: the final body does not decode: native B-rep: unknown variant 'blend', expected one of 'plane', ..., 'placed_revolution'`.

SolidCraft 0.44 writes a `blend` surface kind that CamCraft's `.sc` reader (#1456) does not know. Designs without fillets import. Every design with a fillet, round or blend - most real parts - is refused, so the "open SolidCraft files directly" path does not work for them.

Workarounds today: export STEP from SolidCraft (but see the STEP mesh-gap issue the same runs found) or STL.

Done means: a `.sc` design with fillets from the current SolidCraft release imports with the same body as its STEP export (a pinned fixture `.sc` with a blend face, and a test). Track the next SolidCraft surface kinds the same way (the QA runs re-check each SolidCraft release).

body:
Create the pure-Rust crate `crates/gcode` (`camcraft-gcode`) beside `crates/post`.
It parses RS-274/NGC (NISTIR 6556) and ISO 6983 3-axis milling programs into `cl::Toolpath` sections (`crates/cl/src/cl/path.rs`) and a 1-based line map.

## Scope
- Depend only on `camcraft-cl`, `camcraft-geometry`, and `thiserror` (no `boa_engine`, no `flecs_ecs`, no `camcraft-post` dependency).
- Record the new `camcraft-cl` and `camcraft-geometry` crate edges in `docs/decisions/` per `AGENTS.md`.
- Accept dialect configuration and optional machine reference positions from the caller.
- Track modal groups: motion (`G0`, `G1`, `G2`, `G3`, `G80`), plane (`G17`, `G18`, `G19`), distance (`G90`, `G91`), arc center (`G90.1`, `G91.1`), feed mode (`G94`), units (`G20`, `G21`), length offset (`G43 H`, `G49`), work offsets (`G54`..`G59`), and cycle return (`G98`, `G99`).
- Parse `I`/`J`/`K` arcs and `R` radius arcs (`R > 0` minor arc, `R < 0` major arc) in XY, XZ, and YZ planes.
- Expand canned cycles (`G73`, `G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G84`, `G86`, `G89`) into explicit `cl::Move` chains (`crates/sim/src/sim.rs`).
- Handle `T`, `M6`, `S`, `M3`/`M4`/`M5`, `M0`/`M1`/`M2`/`M30`, `G4`, `G61`/`G64`, and `G53`/`G28`/`G30` when reference positions exist.
- Split sections on tool changes and record a 1-based source line number for every move.
- Refuse unknown words, missing unit mode, `G41`/`G42`, macros (`G65`, `M98`, `#`), probing (`G31`, `G38.2`), `R` full circles, and `A`/`B`/`C` words by name with the 1-based line number.
- Add a clean-room provenance comment to each module (`AGENTS.md`).

Done means: `camcraft-gcode` builds in the workspace with a `docs/decisions/` entry, parses 3-axis ISO programs into `cl::Toolpath` sections with a 1-based line map, and tests pin modal tracking, `I`/`J`/`K` and `R` arcs, canned cycles, unit scaling, and named line-numbered refusals.

Part of #2213
